english: Let $D$ be the set of all real numbers $x$ for which both $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x\left(3-x^{2}\right)}{2}\right)$ and $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$ are defined, where $\sin^{-1}$ takes values in $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$. Let $F:D\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $F(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x\left(3-x^{2}\right)}{2}\right)-3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$. If $m$ is the minimum value of $F$ on $D$, then the value of $\dfrac{m}{\pi}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $D$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $x$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x\left(3-x^{2}\right)}{2}\right)$ तथा $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$ दोनों परिभाषित हैं, जहाँ $\sin^{-1}$ के मान $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ में हैं। माना कि $F:D\to\mathbb{R}$, $F(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x\left(3-x^{2}\right)}{2}\right)-3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। यदि $D$ पर $F$ का न्यूनतम मान $m$ है, तो $\dfrac{m}{\pi}$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Domain of the first term: we need $-1\le\dfrac{x(3-x^{2})}{2}\le1$.
Upper bound: $3x-x^{3}\le2\iff x^{3}-3x+2\ge0$. Since $x=1$ is a double root, $x^{3}-3x+2=(x-1)^{2}(x+2)$, which is $\ge0$ exactly when $x\ge-2$.
Lower bound: $3x-x^{3}\ge-2\iff x^{3}-3x-2\le0$, and $x^{3}-3x-2=(x+1)^{2}(x-2)$, which is $\le0$ exactly when $x\le2$.
So the first term is defined on $[-2,2]$; the second needs $|x|\le2$ as well. Hence $D=[-2,2]$.

Substitution: for $x\in[-2,2]$ put $x=2\sin t$ with $t=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2}\in\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$. Then $\dfrac{x(3-x^{2})}{2}=\sin t\,(3-4\sin^{2}t)=\sin3t$, so $F(x)=\sin^{-1}(\sin3t)-3t$ with $3t\in\left[-\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right]$.

Case $\dfrac{\pi}{6}\le t\le\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ ($1\le x\le2$): $\pi-3t\in\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ and $\sin(\pi-3t)=\sin3t$, so $\sin^{-1}(\sin3t)=\pi-3t$ and $F=\pi-6t$. This decreases from $0$ (at $x=1$) to $\pi-3\pi=-2\pi$ (at $x=2$).
Case $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\le t\le-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ ($-2\le x\le-1$): $\sin^{-1}(\sin3t)=-\pi-3t$ and $F=-\pi-6t$, which lies between $0$ and $2\pi$.
So the minimum is attained at the end point $x=2$ of the domain. Direct evaluation confirms it: $F(2)=\sin^{-1}(-1)-3\sin^{-1}(1)=-\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}=-2\pi$.
originality_note: New: the domain of sin^-1(x(3-x^2)/2) is found from the double-root factorisations (x-1)^2(x+2) and (x+1)^2(x-2), and the substitution x = 2 sin t turns the argument into sin 3t, so F is 0 on [-1,1] and its minimum sits at the domain end point (way 5). Closest known: sin^-1(3x-4x^3) = 3 sin^-1 x on [-1/2,1/2]. Different because: the scaling by 2 hides the triple-angle form, the domain must be derived by factorisation, and the question asks for an extremum over the whole domain.

concept_use.Domain and range of inverse trigonometri: The domain [-2,2] comes from -1 <= x(3-x^2)/2 <= 1 via (x-1)^2(x+2) >= 0 and (x+1)^2(x-2) <= 0; the minimum lies at its end point x = 2.
concept_use.Evaluation of inverse trigonometric expr: F(2) = sin^-1(-1) - 3 sin^-1(1) = -2pi and the piecewise values are evaluated with principal ranges.
concept_use.Simplification of Inverse trigonometric: x = 2 sin t gives x(3-x^2)/2 = sin 3t, so F = sin^-1(sin 3t) - 3t piecewise.
